findings.summary: The plan can use the pull request's run, which tests the merge with main rather than the candidate's own tree, so the exact-SHA rule can be met by a result for a different tree.
findings.evidence: `check_and_verify` calls `early_pr` (run/mod.rs:1201) right after the planned CI push, so the same SHA also gets a pull_request run, and it is usually the newer one. `parse_ci_run` picks the newest run named `ci` by `created_at`, with no filter on event or branch. On GitHub, a pull_request run's `head_sha` is the PR head (the candidate), but its checkout is refs/pull/N/merge, the candidate merged with the current base (my understanding of GitHub behaviour, not shown in this snapshot). `resolve` (ci_result.rs:176) checks only `run.sha == sha`, so it passes. The result: a green verdict that covers a different tree, or a red verdict caused by changes on main that rejects correct work. The request is explicit: 'A green run for that exact SHA is used', and that is why the request pushes a dedicated `athena/ci/<job id>` branch. Fix: Make the CI source read only the run from the job's own branch: event `push` and head_branch `athena/ci/<job id>`. For example, build the GhClient-backed source with the branch name and add `&event=push&branch=<branch>` to the `actions/runs` query, or filter `workflow_runs` on `event`/`head_branch` in the parser. Add a `ci_checks_parse_*` fixture with both a pull_request run and a push run for the same SHA, showing that only the push run on the CI branch is chosen. Add a run-level case where only a pull_request run exists and the job falls back to the local checks. Replace the 'either run serves' text in ci.yml and ci-routing.md.
findings.location: Decision 10 and Decision 3 (`GhClient::fetch` takes the newest `ci` run by `created_at`, and either run's aggregate job serves); crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs:519-525, 570-589; crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1201

findings.summary: The reread path calls `self.dispatch(...)` from inside `dispatch`, so after the rename the wrapper would be nested and the branch delete step would run twice.
findings.evidence: run/mod.rs:737 `return self.dispatch(&new_head, &new_records, &new_job, new_reading, accepted_by, Outputs { ui, stages });` inside `fn dispatch`. Fix: Have that recursive call target `dispatch_run`, so `drop_ci_branch` runs once per job, and say so in step 6.
findings.location: Decision 4 / Step 6 (rename `dispatch` to `dispatch_run` plus a wrapper); crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:737

summary: The plan wires `resolve` and `run_routed` in where the gap actually is: `NoCi` is still passed at run/mod.rs:1269. It names real seams (`early_seam`, `gh::Remote::remote_head`/`push`, `https_github_repository`, `LowDisk`, `verify::reuse_statement`), and its demonstrations go through `Athena::go`, so they would fail without the behaviour. Rewriting `parse_ci_run` around the aggregate `ci` job is justified: the current parser copies one step named 'cargo fmt --check' to all three checks, which no longer matches the split jobs in ci.yml. One major soundness flaw remains. Because `early_pr` also opens a pull request for the same SHA, and `fetch` takes the newest `ci` run without filtering on event or branch, the result used will usually be the pull_request run. As far as I know, that run tests the merge with the base branch, not the candidate's exact tree, which defeats the exact-SHA rule the request asks for and can reject correct work. Restricting the source to the push run on `athena/ci/<job id>` fixes it. Athena's own six scope findings were weighed: each extra file has a narrow, stated reason, so they are not repeated here.
